clue.text: Drug-addled President gets judge to replace translator at the beginning of serious events

parts.note: someone drug-addled is high

indicators.note: one thing coming in to replace another signals a swap of letters within the President's name

parts.note: Donald Trump, US President
TR is a standard abbreviation for translator (or translated)
J is the abbreviation for judge, as in legal citations

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word serious is wanted

explanation.surface: A political scandal: a stoned president swaps his interpreter for a judge at the start of grave proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' swaps the TR of TRUMP for J, leaving JUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: High jumps are athletics contests, so they count as sporting events at a meeting.

clue.text: Pipes steeplechasers possibly hand out

indicators.note: out tells us the hand's letter is removed from the runners

parts.note: steeplechases are horse races over fences, so the runners may be horses; 'possibly' flags the example
R stands for right, as in right hand

explanation.surface: Someone hands out pipes to racing horses, or to the people who run steeplechases.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoses are flexible tubes for carrying water, a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Came across gold during a delay up country

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction reads from the bottom upwards
the meeting and the gold sit within a delay, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lag is a delay
came across means met, as in met someone by chance
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A traveller stumbles on gold while held up on the way to some country.
explanation.walkthrough: METAU goes inside ALAG to give ALAMETAUG, which 'up' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a republic in Central America, bordering Mexico.

clue.text: Flag is cheerful, I understand

parts.note: jolly means cheerful; 'is' reads with it in the surface
in radio talk, roger means message received and understood

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges that a flag looks cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the traditional skull-and-crossbones banner flown by pirates.

clue.text: Test mostly cut to pieces during dinner?

indicators.note: the shortened chopping word sits within the dinner

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal, hence the question mark

indicators.note: mostly means take all but the final letter of the chopping word

parts.note: to dice food is to cut it into small cubes

explanation.surface: A dinner guest wonders whether an exam was mostly chopped up during the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination by a doctor, a health test.

clue.text: Spanish men surround Italy's elders

indicators.note: the Spanish men enclose the letter for Italy

parts.note: señores are Spanish gentlemen, written without the tilde
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A group of Spaniards gathers around the older Italians.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniors are people older than others, just as elders are.

clue.text: Article in lower case editor spiked

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the lower case abbreviation

parts.note: LC is the printers' abbreviation for lower case
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor kills a piece written in lower-case letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiked' looks like the editor's rejection of an article, but it means a drink with something added.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink that is spiked or laced has alcohol or a drug secretly added.

clue.text: Vegetable starter for lunch that's scary

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so only the opening letter of lunch is used

parts.note: eek is the cry someone gives at something frightening

explanation.surface: A diner squeals at the first course of lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an onion-family vegetable with a long white stem.

clue.text: Picked a hundred socks

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hose is an old word for stockings and socks

explanation.surface: Someone selects a hundred pairs of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chose is the past tense of choose, the same as picked or selected.

clue.text: Keeping secrets, policeman covers up last note to ruin someone's reputation

indicators.note: the detective covers up the final note of the secretive word, hiding it by taking its place

parts.note: someone discreet keeps secrets to themselves
E is a musical note
DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police

explanation.surface: A corrupt officer hides a final memo while keeping secrets, to wreck someone's good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers up' puts DI over the second E of DISCREET, giving DISCREDIT. DI is a Detective Inspector, a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone is to damage their good standing so they are no longer believed.

clue.text: Second unbelievable delay

parts.note: a tall story is one too far-fetched to be believed

explanation.surface: A second hold-up is hard to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time, putting something off.

clue.text: It's risky showing emotion during party with us

indicators.note: the emotion goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party or social occasion
anger is a strong emotion

explanation.surface: A warning that losing your temper at a party with us around is asking for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous carries risk of harm, so it is risky.

clue.text: Chelsea worry about dropping each player

indicators.note: about signals that the remaining letters are turned around and rearranged
dropping means the letters for each are taken out of the football club and worry

explanation.surface: Chelsea football fans fret about losing a player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes EA from CHELSEA WORRY, leaving CHLSWORRY plus E to give CHLSEWORRY; 'about' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheryl Crow is an American singer-songwriter and guitarist, so a musical player.

clue.text: Fruit and veg right

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A shopping list of fruit and vegetables, ticked off as correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a sweet orchard fruit related to the apple.

clue.text: Film with everyone stumped about plane?

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the stumped abbreviation goes about, around, the tree

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
the plane is a kind of tree, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Passengers baffled about an aircraft, perhaps in a disaster movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the plane tree. In cricket, ST marks a batsman out stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is Oliver Stone's 1987 movie about New York finance.

clue.text: Where cheese may be put having continued success

definitions.meaning: a filling of cheese might go in a bread bun
doing well again and again, in a winning streak

explanation.surface: A cheese sandwich and a winning streak share the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese can be served in a bread bun, and someone enjoying a streak of wins is said to be in that state.

clue.text: Wild bears on TV following rules

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wildlife documentaries show untamed bears on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Being observant of rules means obeying or keeping them, as with religious customs.

clue.text: Treated unfairly back in Slough

indicators.note: the back of the ship goes inside the casting-off word

parts.note: to slough is to cast off, as a snake sheds its skin
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being badly treated back in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town west of London; here it is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shafted, in informal English, is to be cheated or treated unjustly.

clue.text: One of Shakespeare's sisters put up with precious pre-adolescent

parts.note: precious and twee both mean affectedly dainty or quaint

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the sister's name is written upwards

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's three daughters, with Goneril and Cordelia

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean heroine tolerates a fussy, precious child.
explanation.definitionFit: A child aged roughly ten to twelve, between childhood and the teens, is a tween or pre-teen.

clue.text: Escorted by Nazis, former tennis champion drools

indicators.note: the tennis player is flanked on both sides by the Nazi letters

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation
Rod Laver, Australian winner of two calendar Grand Slams

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star, guarded by Nazis, drools.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, so slavers matches drools as a verb.

clue.text: Oil company gets bill for resin

parts.note: Shell is a major oil company
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: A petroleum giant is invoiced for a supply of resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin secreted by the lac insect, used in varnish.

clue.text: Financially sound star let off steam

parts.note: Sol is the Sun, our star
to vent is to release pent-up feelings

explanation.surface: A wealthy celebrity has a rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent person or firm can pay all their debts.

clue.text: Only flatulence for old trick

indicators.note: one thing given in place of another, so the gas takes the place of the old letter

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
wind is a polite word for intestinal gas

explanation.surface: A joker relies on nothing but breaking wind for a stale prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts WIND in place of the O in SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fraud or con, a deceitful trick to get money.

clue.text: Exercises agents

definitions.meaning: repeated lifts or movements in a gym set
short for representatives, especially sales agents

explanation.surface: Gym workouts and sales staff share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reps means repetitions of a gym exercise, and also sales representatives who act as agents.

clue.text: Having overtaken English, stick

parts.note: a car that has overtaken another has gone past it

explanation.surface: A driver passes an Englishman and then gets stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is a glue, and to paste is to stick things together.

clue.text: Republican sees I can't organise opposition

indicators.note: organise asks for these letters to be put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A US Republican admits defeat at organising the opposing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of opposing or fighting back against something.

clue.text: Peers in Court?

parts.note: Read as nobles at court, it names a rank of peer

explanation.surface: Members of the nobility appear in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl's Court is a district of west London, formerly home to a big exhibition centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are nobles of the British peerage, and they precede Court in the London place name.

clue.text: Terse report from survivor is out of control

definitions.meaning: a clipped I-am-fine message, dropping the I

explanation.surface: A survivor's brief message is wildly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: A survivor might signal just AM OK, a clipped version of I am OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave in a wild, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Put together when steam oddly leaked

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the vapour word

parts.note: colours or ink that leaked have bled

explanation.surface: Machinery was put together at the moment steam strangely escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled means built from parts, put together.

clue.text: Time to stop queen being keen

indicators.note: the period stops up the queen's letters, sitting between them like a plug

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone eager to see the queen stopped in her tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen both mean full of enthusiasm and wanting to do something.

clue.text: First of the feeble make slight change

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word the is wanted

parts.note: feeble and weak both mean lacking strength

explanation.surface: The feeblest make only small adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak something is to adjust it a little.

clue.text: US caterer's stuffed animals

indicators.note: stuffed suggests the letters are crammed together in a jumble

explanation.surface: An American caterer's animals have been stuffed, by a taxidermist or with food.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', a link; the anagram is of US CATERER alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures are living beings, especially animals.
